server: Web research tools for agents: search, read, crawl, extract, and watch web pages, with typed inputs and capped output. No API key needed.

tools.search: Search the web, Wikipedia, Hacker News, or arXiv without an API key. Use it to find pages on a topic. Returns titles, URLs, and snippets.
tools.scrape: Read one web page as clean Markdown, without menus or ads. Use it when you have a URL and need its text. Returns the page title and Markdown.
tools.map: List the URLs on a site from its sitemap and links. Use it to see what pages a site has before you scrape. Returns a list of URLs.
tools.summarize: Pick the key sentences from a text or a web page, with no model call. Pass text or url. Returns the top sentences.
tools.crawl: Visit a page and the pages it links to, up to a depth and a page limit. Use it to read a small part of a site at once. Returns each page's URL and Markdown.
tools.extract: Get named parts of a page with CSS selectors, like a price or a title. Pass fields as name:selector pairs, or one selector. Returns the matched text.
tools.answer: Answer a question from a few web sources, with no model call. Use it for a quick fact with sources. Pass urls to read only those pages, with no search. Returns the key sentences and the URLs they came from.
tools.research: Look into a topic across many web sources. Use it when one search is not enough. Returns key points with their source URLs.
tools.parse: Turn a local file, like a PDF or an HTML file, into clean text. Use it when the content is on disk, not on the web. Returns the text.
tools.media: Save a page's media to a file: download it, take a screenshot, or print a PDF. Use it when you need the file itself. Returns where the file was saved and its size.
tools.monitor: Check a page for changes since the last check. Use it to watch a page over time. Returns whether it changed and what changed.
tools.batch: Scrape many URLs in one call. Use it when you already have a list of pages. Returns one result per URL, each marked ok or not.
tools.act: Open a page in a real browser and read it, with an optional screenshot. Use it for pages that need JavaScript to show their text. Returns the page text. Or pass goal instead of url to act in the Cua window named by WEBULAR_CUA_WINDOW, such as goal: click "Press me" until it says "Done". Then it returns status (done or infeasible), at (the step it could not reach), and rungs (how each step was clicked: ax, ocr, or pixel).
tools.feed: Read an RSS or Atom feed. Use it to get the newest posts from a site. Returns each item's title, link, and date.
tools.doctor: Check that webular can run on this computer. Use it when a webular tool fails for no clear reason. Returns each check, whether it passed, and a short note.
tools.tasks: List the mise tasks that webular runs through. Use it to see how webular builds, checks, and runs its commands. Returns the task names and how many there are.
tools.diagram: List the XState machines that model how webular commands run. Use it to see which flows webular models. Returns the machine names and how many there are.
tools.audit: Check whether deepsec is installed and show the security scan plan, with no API key. Use it before you run a security scan. Returns whether deepsec is ready and the command to run.

titles.answer: Answer a question from the web
titles.media: Save page media to a file
titles.act: Open a page in a browser
